svg.text: Visual conventions: MySQL Workbench 26.7 · Data and analysis: myflames
select d.dept_name AS dept_name,round(AVG(s.salary),2) AS avg_salary
where ((s.emp_no = de.emp_no) and (d.dept_no = de.dept_no) and (de.to_date = DATE'9999-01-01') and (s.to_date = DATE'9999-01-01'))
Data flows downward. Colors identify operators; arrow width represents estimated rows on a log scale.
Join circles show the reported join type: left joins include the whole left circle; inner joins highlight the overlap.
Select a node for details. Drag to pan, scroll gently to zoom, or use Fit plan and the zoom buttons.
Row estimate off by 10× or more: salaries (estimated 1, actual 11 rows per loop, 11× under)
1 sort operation(s) — 9 rows; may use disk-based filesort
• Refresh statistics with ANALYZE TABLE salaries. If a filter on a non-indexed column stays misestimated, add a histogram: on MySQL 8.0+, ANALYZE TABLE salaries UPDATE
HISTOGRAM ON <column> WITH 100 BUCKETS; on MariaDB, ANALYZE TABLE salaries PERSISTENT FOR COLUMNS (<column>) INDEXES (). Why: the optimizer picks join order and access methods
from these estimates. InnoDB recalculates persistent statistics on its own only after about 10% of a table's rows change, and on MariaDB, under the default
use_stat_tables=PREFERABLY_FOR_QUERIES, ANALYZE TABLE collects column statistics and histograms only when you add PERSISTENT FOR.
• Add indexes on filter/join columns to avoid full table scans
• Increase sort_buffer_size or add an ordered index to avoid filesort
